title: Company Case Study: Binance's $6.34B hack began with a fake job interview
description:
On October 29, 2026, attackers drained hot wallets at Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange. Binance puts the impact at about $6.34 billion in digital assets. This case study looks at how the company responded, what it admitted, and what it says it fixed.

What happened
- 233.46 million XRP left five Binance hot wallets in about four minutes; the last unauthorized transfer came nearly four hours later (Binance's initial findings).

Binance's decisions
1. Stop the bleeding: withdrawals were paused, the attacker's hold on a hot wallet was cleared, and law enforcement and blockchain tracing firms were called in. Withdrawals reopened in phases from November 1.
2. Users don't carry the loss: Binance says about $2.85 billion is frozen or intercepted, that it will absorb the losses, and that 98% of affected token assets were replenished as of October 31.
3. Explain it within five days: Binance published its initial findings on November 3. The investigation is ongoing and a full technical report is still to come.

How the attackers got in (per Binance)
- June: a wallet engineer installed a tampered copy of Homebrew, a developer tool. Binance detected it and replaced the device, but the attackers had learned about the wallet team.
- September: a second engineer went through fake job interviews and downloaded a coding assignment that hid malware. Binance says its endpoint security tools did not detect it at the time.
- October 20: an internal AI tool was abused to take control of two more engineers' computers.
- October 29: a stolen container deployment token was used to deploy a container and start the theft.

Binance described it as "not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident". It says it rebuilt the wallet system and the AI tool's access controls, replaced devices, shut down affected credentials and tokens, and plans an independent review.

Attribution: the FBI attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean group it also tied to the $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025. North Korea denies it.

Analyst note (Securidge analysis): the weak point was a laptop, not the blockchain.

What to do this week
1. Never run job interview tasks on a work laptop.
2. Install developer tools only from official sources.
3. Keep deployment tokens off everyday laptops.
4. Alert on unusual wallet or payment actions.

Sources
- Binance, "29 October Binance Security Incident: Initial Findings and Response Update" (Nov 3, 2026): https://x.com/binance/status/2117626126214504729
- The Register (Nov 3, 2026): https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/03/north-korean-fake-job-interview-led-to-63b-binance-heist/5307398
- Help Net Security (Nov 4, 2026): https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/04/binance-hack-north-korea-fake-job-interview/
- The Hacker News (Nov 2026): https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/binance-reveals-how-fake-job-interviews.html
- ITV News / AP, FBI attribution (Oct 31, 2026): https://www.itv.com/news/2026-10-31/fbi-says-north-korean-hackers-behind-binance-crypto-heist
